Text with descriptions about the conference such as '5 minutes, 20 slides' and '18 amazing presenters', appears over the video.

activities.description: Alena Chang walks onto the stage and begins her presentation.
Alena Chang talks about the meaning and impact of names, particularly for minorities.
Alena Chang shares personal anecdotes about her own experience with her Korean name.
Alena Chang discusses the split-identity phenomenon of many Asian-Americans having both an English and an ethnic name.
Alena Chang examines the evolution of black names and the rise of distinctly black names as a statement of empowerment.
Alena Chang analyzes the relationship between names and class, noting how names trickle down from higher to lower socio-economic classes.
Alena Chang talks about gender neutral names and the gender pay gap.
Alena Chang highlights the double standard surrounding gender-neutral names.
Alena Chang concludes her presentation by emphasizing the significance of names and how they are used to judge people.

narrativeProgression.description: Alena introduces the topic by stating that names embody us and that societies have evolved in their name choices.
Alena shares personal anecdotes about her Korean name and the difficulty Americans had pronouncing it.
Alena discusses the split-identity phenomenon among Asian-Americans with English and ethnic names.
Alena highlights the evolution of black names and the emergence of distinctly black names as a statement of empowerment.
Alena links names to class, explaining how they trickle down from higher to lower socioeconomic groups.
Alena touches on the gender pay gap and the trend of giving children gender-neutral names.
Alena points out the double standard regarding gender-neutral names, with girls adopting boys' names but not vice versa.
Alena concludes her presentation by emphasizing that names are reflections of our backgrounds and identities and that we often use them to judge people.

youtube_description:
Names universally hold a lot of significance. Parents love thinking that their love and guidance are manifested in their lovely Faith or Hope or Joy (I was going to mention Diamond, but I didn't want to turn this into a list of stripper stage names). However, the name-making as a whole brings up many questions regarding the origins and reasoning behind the process. How did America even go from Prudence and Chastity to Temptress and LaFawnda.

Presenter: Alena Chang

Biography:

I wasn't always Alena; I was born Hye-Soo Chang. Heh. Soo. It means wisdom and grace or something. I think it also translates into "graceful bead". I don't even know. Either way, I later chose to change my name to Alena; still not very American-sounding, but at least I don't have to deal with as much crap as before. I still miss Hye-Soo sometimes.
